title: SSE HTTP/2 downgrade & chunk-boundary projection adapter
creator: Leah Moreno
description: Implement an edge-side adapter that normalizes streaming responses for legacy SSE clients when upstream traffic is carried over HTTP/2 (or via buffering proxies). Some customers use HTTP/2-capable load balancers or language runtimes that coalesce frames, causing chunk boundaries to be lost for SSE consumers. The adapter projects deterministic chunk boundaries, preserves function-calling/structured-output delimiters, and exposes a reconnect-safe idempotency token to enable client rejoin without losing message atomicity.
acceptance_criteria: Edge adapter can accept a streaming response from upstream over HTTP/2 and emit valid text/event-stream SSE that adheres to current client expectations (event,id,data blocks).
Chunk boundary projection must preserve original logical events (function-call/structured-output markers) in 99.9% of synthetic workloads in CI with no reordering.
Adapter must expose a stable resume token (X-Stream-Session / SSE id) in the first event and in reconnect handshake that allows client to resume from last-acked event id.
End-to-end latency increase measured at p95 must remain < 15ms for steady-state 512-token responses on canary nodes for typical internal benchmarks.
Observability: add Grafana panels for adapter error-rate, flush-rate, buffering-time, and per-client resume-failure-rate.
Integration tests added that simulate common buffering proxies (ALB, CloudFront, Envoy) and verify adapter behavior under chunk coalescing and TCP stalls.
implementation_notes: Place adapter in edge-proxy (envoy filter) as a streaming filter that rewrites DATA frames into SSE event blocks rather than as an upstream application change.

Chunk projection algorithm: use heuristics based on newline/JSON boundary tokens, function-call sentinel markers (<<FUNC_START/END>>), and max-window timers (e.g., 12ms boundary) to decide safe flush points.

Each projected SSE event will include: 'id: <monotonic-session-seq>' and 'data: <base64-encoded-chunk>' and an 'event: partial' for intermediate fragments. Finalized semantic boundaries (function call closed / structured JSON completed) will emit 'event: committed' with an explicit 'scope' metadata line.

Resume semantics: adapter emits a stable session id header (X-Stream-Session) once per connection. Clients can reconnect with 'Last-Event-ID' to request replay from last acked id. Replay semantics are best-effort within configured retention (default 30s), otherwise fallback to compatibility no-replay.

Backpressure: respect client write buffer; if downstream stalls, adapter buffers up to 2MB per-client and will signal upstream to slow-down via HTTP/2 WINDOW_UPDATE adjustments where possible. If buffer exceeded, emit a controlled terminal event 'event: stall' with code and close connection to avoid resource exhaustion.
Compatibility: when upstream already emits SSE (text/event-stream) over HTTP/1.1, adapter should be a no-op and pass-through headers. The filter must detect content-type and switch modes.
test_plan: Unit tests for chunk projection heuristics (newline-splitting, sentinel detection, window timer).
Integration tests against Envoy-based local proxy replicating ALB/CloudFront buffering behavior.
Chaos test: induce network stalls and random coalescing to verify idempotent replay and client-visible semantics.
Load test: synthetic workload with 10k concurrent streaming clients on canary to validate memory bounds and p95 latency goal.
Security: fuzz header parsing and session token handling; run internal SAST on new filter code.
rollout_plan: Feature-flag the adapter (edge.sse_http2_adapter) default=off in staging.
Deploy to staging cluster, run full e2e suite, and measure metrics for 48 hours.
Canary rollout to 5% of production traffic with telemetry enabled, evaluate for 72 hours. If metrics stable, expand to 25% then 100% over 4 days.
If resume-failure-rate > 0.1% or memory pressure > 70%, rollback to previous flag state.
Post-rollout: schedule a one-week observation window and collect customer feedback for any legacy client issues.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Heuristic mis-splits may break function call atomicity. Mitigation: conservative defaults preferring larger fragments near synthetic boundaries; add opt-in strict-mode for customers that need exact semantics.

Risk: Memory blow-up from many slow clients. Mitigation: per-client soft limits and early-stall events that yield controlled disconnects; track with alerting and automated scale-up policy for edge pool.
Risk: Proxies that rebuffer despite adapter. Mitigation: document supported proxy configs; provide troubleshooting guide and fallbacks (client-side reconnect helper).
comments: 2026-03-02 Leah Moreno: Kicked off spike — ran quick experiments with Envoy filter and confirmed ALB coalesces small DATA frames into large writes; naive pass-through fails client tests.

2026-03-04 Arjun Patel: Prototype implements timer-based flush (10ms) + sentinel detection. Initial results: p95 latency +6ms, memory within budget on box. Pushed prototype PR for early review. (/pull/1423)
2026-03-06 PM review (Samir K): Prefer session resume over guaranteed replay; customers care more about deterministic ordering than complete replay. Adjusted acceptance criteria accordingly.

2026-03-08 Design review (Maya R): Suggested explicit 'committed' event for structured-output boundaries instead of relying only on id gaps — reduces client parsing complexity. Implemented in prototype.
2026-03-10 Security note (June H): Reviewed header handling; session token generation should use HMAC with rotation via KMS. Added to implementation notes and SAST task.

2026-03-12 Arjun Patel: Integration tests for CloudFront buffering added. Observed a 0.03% transient resume_failure at 5% canary due to clock skew in session id generator — fixed by switching to monotonic sequence per-connection.
2026-03-13 Leah Moreno: Ready for staging rollout behind feature flag. Next: finalize Grafana panels and alert thresholds, complete canary runbook.
